title: It's time investors rethink the developed-emerging market divide
gist: UBS's emerging-markets CIO argues that MSCI- and JP Morgan-defined developed/emerging market classifications are increasingly disconnected from reality, citing income levels, industrial leadership, central bank credibility and fiscal discipline where several 'emerging' economies now outperform 'developed' peers, while real gaps persist mainly in capital market depth.

themes.theme: Index-based EM/DM classifications no longer match reality

insights.claim: Investors who rely on outdated emerging market classifications risk missing the most dynamic investment opportunities of the coming decade.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Portfolios built on legacy index-provider classifications may be systematically underweight the fastest-growing parts of the global economy.
insights.quote: Investors who rely on outdated emerging market classifications risk missing the most dynamic opportunities of the decade ahead.
insights.locator: The median inflation rate across the 24 countries

insights.claim: Trillions of dollars in global investment track emerging-market indices built on proprietary classification frameworks run primarily by MSCI (equities) and JP Morgan (fixed income and currencies), and investors are starting to question whether these frameworks still reflect the world as it is today.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A shift in how major index providers classify countries could trigger large capital reallocations across passive and benchmarked strategies.
insights.locator: Globally, investors have long relied on a handful of index providers

insights.claim: The UAE, South Korea and Czechia are still classified as emerging markets despite having income levels comparable to, or even higher than, developed-market countries such as Spain, Italy or New Zealand.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Income-based intuitions about which countries are 'emerging' are already outdated, suggesting index reclassification risk (and associated flows) for these markets.
insights.locator: Questioning the developed vs emerging markets divide

insights.claim: The next decade will favor investors who recognize that the boundary between developed and emerging markets is fading, embrace the new reality, and reposition portfolios accordingly, since today's emerging markets may become tomorrow's leaders.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A call to actively re-underwrite country allocations rather than rely on static developed/emerging buckets.
insights.quote: The next decade will belong to those who recognize this shift, embrace new realities and position their portfolios for a world where yesterday’s “emerging” markets are tomorrow’s leaders.

themes.theme: Industrial and technology leadership has shifted to 'emerging' economies

insights.claim: Taiwan and Korea lead global semiconductor production and are powering the global artificial intelligence revolution, with no competing countries coming close to their capacity.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: AI supply-chain exposure is concentrated in economies still labeled 'emerging,' making them structurally important, not peripheral, plays on the AI buildout.
insights.locator: Attention then shifts to the structure of the economy

insights.claim: Brazil's advanced aerospace industry has produced the world's best-selling executive jet for the last 14 consecutive years.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Illustrates durable, high-value manufacturing competitiveness in an 'emerging' market rather than reliance on commodities alone.

insights.claim: China's operational stock of roughly 2 million industrial robots is almost five times larger than Japan's.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Points to China's scale advantage in industrial automation as a competitiveness and productivity signal that outdated classifications obscure.
insights.locator: China’s operational stock of about 2 million industrial robots

insights.claim: Turkey has become one of the world's leading exporters of military drones.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Highlights a defense-technology export niche emerging outside traditional developed-market defense suppliers.
insights.locator: Turkey has become one of the leading exporters

themes.theme: Emerging market central banks have built inflation-fighting credibility

insights.claim: When inflation spiked after COVID-19, emerging market central banks responded proactively by raising rates well ahead of their developed-market peers, solidifying their inflation-fighting credentials, with Latin American central banks -- carrying fresh memories of past inflationary episodes -- among the most proactive globally.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: EM central bank policy credibility has converged toward, or exceeded, that of developed-market peers, reducing a traditional EM risk premium.

insights.claim: The median inflation rate across the 24 countries in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index was about 2.5% in 2025, lower than in many developed economies.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Lower relative inflation undercuts the standard assumption that emerging markets carry structurally higher macro instability than developed markets.

themes.theme: Fiscal discipline has reversed between developed and emerging economies

insights.claim: When asked to compare fiscal responsibility between a group of 'emerging' countries (Chile, Poland, Malaysia) and a group of 'developed' countries (the US, France, Japan) using variables including debt-to-GDP, deficit-to-GDP, interest-to-revenue, debt maturity and currency mix, institutional credibility, market access and borrowing costs, an AI model concluded that Chile, Malaysia and Poland were the more fiscally responsible group.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A systematic, multi-variable comparison -- not just anecdote -- shows several investment-grade emerging sovereigns now score better on fiscal sustainability than major developed economies.
insights.quote: Bottom-line winners: Chile, Malaysia and Poland.

insights.claim: The IMF estimates Argentina, a high-yield rated sovereign, will deliver a primary fiscal surplus of 1.4% of GDP this year, a result that is nearly impossible to find anywhere in the developed world today.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Fiscal turnaround stories in high-yield EM sovereigns can outpace developed-market fiscal trajectories, a potential re-rating catalyst for EM credit.

insights.claim: Improved fiscal and monetary discipline in emerging markets has helped curb the boom-bust cycles of previous decades and produced more stable inflation outcomes, exemplified by the roughly 2.5% median MSCI EM inflation rate in 2025.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Reduced boom-bust volatility supports a lower structural risk premium for EM assets over time.
insights.locator: This shift has helped curb the boom-bust cycles

themes.theme: Political risk is no longer a distinguishing feature of emerging markets

insights.claim: High political uncertainty, historically viewed as a defining feature of emerging markets, is now widespread across all geographies, with elections in North America and Europe becoming nail-biting, market-moving events.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Political-risk premia once applied narrowly to EM assets should logically be reassessed for developed markets as well.

themes.theme: Capital market depth remains the real developed-emerging divide, but currency volatility is converging

insights.claim: The median emerging market country accounts for just 0.1% of global equity market capitalization, and even the largest emerging market still represents only around 3%.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Capital market depth -- not income, industry, inflation or fiscal discipline -- is the area where the developed/emerging gap genuinely persists, implying liquidity and capacity constraints for large allocators.
insights.locator: One area where differences between developed and emerging markets remain significant

insights.claim: Shallower capital markets tend to experience greater price swings, which is why equity market volatility in emerging markets remains structurally higher than in developed markets.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Even as macro fundamentals converge, EM equity investors should still expect higher volatility purely from market-structure effects.
insights.locator: Shallower capital markets tend to experience

insights.claim: Since the start of 2025, volatility in emerging market currencies has trended lower and, on average, now sits below that of G7 currencies.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A reversal of the traditional EM-currency-risk premium narrative, relevant for FX hedging costs and carry-trade positioning.
